paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates coverage as a function of the number of completions (k), with the x-axis representing k on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ to 2⁸ (i.e., 1 to 256), marked at intervals of 2⁰, 2¹, ..., 2⁸. The y-axis represents coverage, scaled linearly from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick marks at 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8. Four models are compared: Llama-3B (blue solid line with circular markers), Llama-3B + FT (dark green solid line with triangular markers), Llama-1B (light blue dashed line with circular markers), and Llama-1B + FT (light green dashed line with triangular markers). All four lines exhibit a monotonically increasing trend in coverage as k increases. The Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT lines begin at approximately 0.42 coverage at k=1 and rise to roughly 0.92 at k=256, with the two lines being nearly indistinguishable across the entire range. The Llama-1B line starts near 0.22 at k=1 and increases to about 0.72 at k=128, showing minimal further improvement beyond that point. The Llama-1B + FT line also begins near 0.22 but consistently remains above the base Llama-1B line, reaching approximately 0.77 at k=256, demonstrating a persistent ~5 percentage point advantage from fine-tuning.
